   154→   // Memory stage
   155→   RAM data_memory(
   156→     .address(alu_result_mem[11:0]),
   157→     .data_in(data_readRegB_mem),
   158→     .write_enable(ctrl_memWrite),
   159→     .clock(clock),
   160→     .data_out(mem_data)
   161→   );
   162→
   163→   // Select: memory data (load) or ALU result (other)
   164→   wire [31:0] wb_data = ctrl_memToReg ? mem_data : alu_result_mem;
   165→   ```
   166→
   167→   **Stage 5: Write Back (WB)**
   168→   - Writes the result back to the register file
   169→   - Destination register comes from rd (R-type) or rt (I-type loads)
   170→   - Write enable asserted for instructions that produce a result
   171→   - Connects back to the register file write port
   172→
   173→   Verilog snippet:

   176→   assign ctrl_writeEnable = reg_write_wb;
   177→   assign ctrl_writeReg = dest_reg_wb;
   178→   assign data_writeReg = wb_data_wb;
   179→   ```

   181→3. **Pipeline Registers** - The glue between stages:
   182→   - IF/ID register: holds instruction and PC+1
   183→   - ID/EX register: holds decoded values, control signals, register data
   184→   - EX/MEM register: holds ALU result, memory write data, control signals
   185→   - MEM/WB register: holds final data to write back, control signals
   186→   - All pipeline registers are edge-triggered D flip-flops
   187→   - Flush and stall control for hazards
   188→
   189→   Verilog snippet:
   190→   ```verilog
   191→   // IF/ID Pipeline Register
   192→   reg [31:0] ifid_instruction, ifid_pc_plus_one;
   193→
   194→   always @(posedge clock or posedge reset) begin
   195→     if (reset || flush_ifid) begin
   196→       ifid_instruction <= 32'b0;  // NOP
   197→       ifid_pc_plus_one <= 32'b0;
   198→     end else if (!stall) begin
   199→       ifid_instruction <= instruction;
   200→       ifid_pc_plus_one <= pc_plus_one;
   201→     end
   202→   end
   203→   ```
   204→
   205→4. **Control Unit** - Generating control signals:
   206→   - Opcode-based decoding: each opcode maps to a set of control signals
   207→   - Control signals: RegWrite, MemWrite, MemToReg, ALUSrc, Branch, Jump, ALUOp
   208→   - Table of control signals per instruction type:
   209→     - R-type (00000): RegWrite=1, ALUSrc=0
   210→     - addi (00101): RegWrite=1, ALUSrc=1
   211→     - lw (01000): RegWrite=1, MemToReg=1, ALUSrc=1
   212→     - sw (00111): MemWrite=1, ALUSrc=1
   213→     - beq (00010): Branch=1
   214→     - bne (00110): Branch=1
   215→     - j (00001): Jump=1
   216→     - jal (00011): RegWrite=1, Jump=1

   236→   .stage-wb { background: #66bb6a; color: white; font-weight: 600; }
   237→   ```

    73→   - Hazards are situations where the next instruction cannot execute in the next clock cycle

    75→   - This processor primarily handles data hazards and control hazards

    78→
    79→2. **Data Hazards** - Read-After-Write (RAW) dependencies:
    80→   - Occurs when an instruction needs a value that a previous instruction has not yet written back
    81→   - Example scenario using the instruction timeline:

    83→     add $1, $2, $3    // writes $1 in WB (cycle 5)
    84→     sub $4, $1, $5    // reads $1 in ID (cycle 3) - STALE VALUE!

    86→   - Without forwarding: the sub instruction reads the OLD value of $1
    87→   - Show a timeline diagram (using CSS grid similar to pipeline page):

    90→     add $1:   IF   ID   EX   MEM  WB  <-- $1 written here
    91→     sub $4:        IF   ID   EX   MEM <-- $1 read here (too early!)
    92→     ```
    93→
    94→   Use colored cells to highlight the conflict.
    95→
    96→3. **Data Forwarding (Bypassing)** - The primary solution:
    97→   - Instead of waiting for WB, forward the result from where it is computed
    98→   - EX-to-EX forwarding: forward ALU result from EX/MEM register to EX stage input
    99→   - MEM-to-EX forwarding: forward data from MEM/WB register to EX stage input

   106→                    && (exmem_rd == idex_rs);
   107→   wire ex_hazard_B = (exmem_regWrite && exmem_rd != 0)
   108→                    && (exmem_rd == idex_rt);
   109→

   112→                     && !(exmem_regWrite && exmem_rd == idex_rs)
   113→                     && (memwb_rd == idex_rs);
   114→   wire mem_hazard_B = (memwb_regWrite && memwb_rd != 0)
   115→                     && !(exmem_regWrite && exmem_rd == idex_rt)
   116→                     && (memwb_rd == idex_rt);
   117→   ```

   142→   - Solution: insert a pipeline bubble (NOP) and stall IF/ID register for 1 cycle

   139→   | sll $rd, $rs, shamt | 00100 | rd = rs << shamt | Shift left logical |

   148→   | sw $rd, imm($rs)   | 00111 | Mem[rs + imm] = rd | Store word |
   149→   | beq $rd, $rs, imm  | 00010 | if(rd==rs) PC+=imm | Branch if equal |
   150→   | bne $rd, $rs, imm  | 00110 | if(rd!=rs) PC+=imm | Branch if not equal |

   219→1. **Overview** - Memory in the processor:
   220→   - Harvard architecture: separate instruction memory (ROM) and data memory (RAM)
   221→   - Instruction memory is read-only (loaded with program at synthesis)
   222→   - Data memory is read/write (for load and store instructions)
   223→   - Both memories are word-addressed (32-bit words)
   224→   - Memory address space: 12-bit addresses (4096 words)
   225→
   226→2. **Instruction Memory (ROM)** - Read-only program storage:
   227→   - Contains the assembled program binary
   228→   - Addressed by the Program Counter (PC)
   229→   - Combinational read (no clock delay): instruction available same cycle as address
   230→   - In simulation: initialized from a .mem or .mif file
   231→   - In synthesis: compiled into FPGA block RAM
   232→
   233→   Verilog snippet:
   234→   ```verilog
   235→   // Instruction Memory (ROM)
   236→   module ROM(
   237→     input [11:0] address,
   238→     output [31:0] data
   239→   );
   240→     reg [31:0] memory [0:4095];
   241→
   242→     initial begin
   243→       $readmemh("program.mem", memory);
   244→     end
   245→
   246→     assign data = memory[address];
   247→   endmodule
   248→   ```
   249→
   250→3. **Data Memory (RAM)** - Read/write data storage:
   251→   - Used by load (lw) and store (sw) instructions
   252→   - Synchronous write: data written on clock edge
   253→   - Combinational read: data available same cycle (or synchronous with 1-cycle latency)
   254→   - Write enable controlled by the memory stage
   255→
   256→   Verilog snippet:
   257→   ```verilog
   258→   // Data Memory (RAM)
   259→   module RAM(
   260→     input [11:0] address,
   261→     input [31:0] data_in,
   262→     input write_enable,
   263→     input clock,
   264→     output [31:0] data_out
   265→   );
   266→     reg [31:0] memory [0:4095];
   267→
   268→     always @(posedge clock) begin
   269→       if (write_enable)
   270→         memory[address] <= data_in;
   271→     end
   272→
   273→     assign data_out = memory[address];
   274→   endmodule
   275→   ```
   276→
   277→4. **Memory Map** - Address space layout:
   278→   - Table showing:
   279→     - 0x000 - 0xFFF: Instruction Memory (ROM) - 4096 words
   280→     - 0x000 - 0xFFF: Data Memory (RAM) - 4096 words (separate address space)
   281→   - Harvard architecture means separate address buses
   282→   - No memory-mapped I/O in this design
   283→
   284→5. **Wrapper Module** - Top-level connection:
   285→   - The `Wrapper.v` module connects processor, ROM, and RAM
   286→   - Processor outputs memory addresses and data
   287→   - Wrapper routes signals to appropriate memory modules
   288→   - Clock and reset distributed from wrapper
   289→
   290→   Verilog snippet:
   291→   ```verilog
   292→   // Top-level Wrapper connecting processor to memories
   293→   module Wrapper(
   294→     input clock, reset
   295→   );
   296→     wire [31:0] instruction, pc;
   297→     wire [31:0] mem_address, mem_data_in, mem_data_out;
   298→     wire mem_write_enable;
   299→
   300→     // Instruction Memory
   301→     ROM imem(.address(pc[11:0]), .data(instruction));
   302→
   303→     // Data Memory
   304→     RAM dmem(
   305→       .address(mem_address[11:0]),
   306→       .data_in(mem_data_in),
   307→       .write_enable(mem_write_enable),
   308→       .clock(clock),
   309→       .data_out(mem_data_out)
   310→     );
   311→
   312→     // Processor
   313→     processor cpu(
   314→       .clock(clock), .reset(reset),
   315→       .instruction(instruction),
   316→       .pc(pc),
   317→       .mem_address(mem_address),
   318→       .mem_data_in(mem_data_in),
   319→       .mem_data_out(mem_data_out),
   320→       .mem_write_enable(mem_write_enable)
   321→     );
   322→   endmodule
   323→   ```
   324→
   325→6. **Memory in the Simulator** - How the JavaScript demo models memory:
   326→   - Instruction memory: array of instruction objects with opcode/operand fields
   327→   - Data memory: Uint32Array of 256 words (simplified from 4096)
   328→   - Memory view component shows non-zero addresses

   356→```

#### Phase 13: Documentation Foundation
**Goal**: Comprehensive CPU documentation covering all major components following Duke ECE 350 checkpoint progression (ALU, Register File, MultDiv, Pipeline, Hazards, Instructions, Memory)
**Depends on**: Phase 11
**Requirements**: DOC-01, DOC-02, DOC-03, DOC-04, DOC-07, DOC-08
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
  1. CPU project has landing page explaining the project and linking to demo and all doc topics
  2. ALU Design documentation explains Carry-Lookahead adder implementation (CP1)
  3. Register File documentation explains 32-register design with $0 hardwired to zero (CP2)
  4. MultDiv documentation explains Booth's multiplication algorithm (CP3)
  5. Pipeline Architecture documentation explains 5-stage pipeline design (CP4)
  6. Hazards & Forwarding documentation explains data hazards and forwarding paths (CP4)
  7. Instruction Set documentation lists all implemented instructions with encoding formats
  8. Memory System documentation explains RAM/ROM and instruction/data memory
  9. All doc pages include Verilog code snippets from actual implementation
  10. All doc pages link to GitHub repo for full source code
**Plans:** 7 plans

Plans:
- [ ] 13-01-PLAN.md — CPU docs landing page + routing setup (DOC-01)
- [ ] 13-02-PLAN.md — ALU Design documentation page (DOC-03, CP1)

   - ALU Design (CP1): "/cpu-docs/alu" - "Carry-Lookahead adder, arithmetic and logic operations"
   - Register File (CP2): "/cpu-docs/regfile" - "32 registers, dual read ports, $0 hardwired to zero"
   - Multiplication & Division (CP3): "/cpu-docs/multdiv" - "Booth's algorithm, 2-layer implementation"
   - Pipeline Architecture (CP4): "/cpu-docs/pipeline" - "5-stage pipeline, datapath design"
   - Hazards & Forwarding (CP4): "/cpu-docs/hazards" - "Data hazards, forwarding paths, stall logic"
   - Instruction Set: "/cpu-docs/instructions" - "Complete instruction reference with encoding formats"
   - Memory System: "/cpu-docs/memory" - "RAM, ROM, instruction and data memory"

   Use React Router `Link` components (not `<a>` tags) for internal navigation.

7. **Quick links section** with:
   - Link to CPU Simulator demo: "/projects/cpu-simulator"
   - Link to GitHub repo: "https://github.com/AaronDiefes/CPU" (external, target="_blank")
   - Link to Portfolio: "/"

8. **Footer** matching DocsPage.jsx pattern (inline styles, same structure with navigation, resources, built-with sections). Update "Built With" to show: Verilog HDL, ModelSim Simulation, Quartus Synthesis, JavaScript Visualization.

9. **Inline CSS** in style tag within the component (same pattern as DocsPage). Reuse the exact same CSS classes: `.landing-header`, `.container`, `.section`, `.pipeline-diagram`, `.pipeline-step`, `.pipeline-arrow`, `.doc-cards`, `.doc-card`, `.quick-links`, `.quick-link`, plus responsive breakpoints at 768px and 480px.
